subject: Greenline Health 3Y contract — request for rate-horizon approval
messages:
From: Sarah Lin <sarah@greenlinehealth.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 8 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Three-year procurement question / budget constraints

Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Greenline’s exec team is aligned on moving forward, but procurement has flagged a budget planning constraint across FY27–29. They asked whether we can get a firm per-token/unit rate for three years (they need predictability for their grant-funded projects). They also want protection so that reasonable model/market-driven price moves don’t surprise their renewal planning.

High-level ask from Greenline: can Redwood provide a three-year commercial with:
- A fixed base unit rate for year 1, then an uplift cap for years 2–3 (they suggested no more than 4% yoy)
- A renewal protection clause allowing an early renewal window if market pricing increases >6% at renewal
- A commitment to data isolation and audit logs (we already covered SOC2)

I’ve attached their internal budget summary for context. Can you confirm feasibility and next steps? They’re hoping to have procurement sign-off by 11/17.

Best,
Sarah
Sarah Lin
Head of Platform Operations
Greenline Health
attachments: Greenline_Budget_2026.pdf

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwoodinference.com>
To: Deal Desk <dealdesk@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 08:03:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Three-year procurement question / budget constraints

Team — forwarding Greenline’s ask. Summary: they want a 3-year commitment with a predictable rate horizon and a renewal protection mechanism. Key commercial asks: fixed Y1 rate, uplift cap <=4% suggested by buyer for Y2–Y3, and renewal-protection if market rises beyond ~6% at renewal. They require SOC2/audit logs (we’re fine).

Why I’m escalating: to meet their procurement timeline (sign-off by 11/17) we need an exec pricing exception for:
- A custom 3-year rate schedule (multi-year discount + firm unit rate year 1)
- Explicit uplift cap language for years 2–3
- Renewal protection clause (limits customer downside at renewal if market price spikes)

Proposed commercial approach (what I’m comfortable proposing to them if we get approval):
- Year 1: $0.0048 / token equivalent (5% net discount to list for commit level)
- Year 2: + capped uplift at max 4% over prior year
- Year 3: + capped uplift at max 4% over prior year
- Renewal protection: customer may early-renew within a 90-day window before renewal at the lower of (a) current list price discounted by their committed discount or (b) our published price if it increased >6% since signing
- Minimum committed spend: $1.2M over 36 months (to protect unit economics)

Attached: commercial summary and draft SOW.
Can you advise: 1) do we have authority to sign this structure (discount + uplift caps + renewal protection) or does this need Ben / exec sign-off? 2) any finance/legal concerns I should surface to Greenline now?

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call.

--
Sofia Ivanova
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sofia_ivanova@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0192
attachments: Greenline_Commercial_Summary.xlsx, Greenline_Draft_SOW_v3.docx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 10:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Three-year procurement question / budget constraints

Sofia — thanks for the clear summary. A few notes from me:
- Finance will want a clear outline of the committed spend and projected unit economics by quarter; the $1.2M over 36 months looks directionally fine but we need to model tail usage.
- Legal will need to scope precise wording for the renewal protection clause — that clause can unintentionally lock us into below-market rates if not tightly scoped (we want a cap on the delta triggering early renewal, and clear definitions of "published price" and applicable model families).
- Given the uplift cap + multi-year commit, this should be an exec approval. Ben — can you weigh in on the allowable discount depth and whether we can accept the proposed uplift caps as-is?

Connor — can you pull a forecast of token consumption for GL (Q1–Q4 2027) so we can present finance with expected utilization and downside scenarios?

Marissa
VP, Sales Operations
--

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Three-year procurement question / budget constraints

Thanks for flagging. I approve moving forward with the structure subject to the following executive conditions:
1) Discount / pricing authorization: approve Year 1 unit at $0.0048 given the $1.2M commit, provided legal adds standard change-of-service language.
2) Uplift caps: authorize up to 4% yoy uplift caps for years 2 and 3 (as proposed) but require a hard ceiling clause that total cumulative uplift cannot exceed 8% across years 2–3.
3) Renewal protection: approve the limited early-renewal protection only if we define an explicit trigger (market movement >6% and only for published base list prices for the model families in scope). Legal to add a carve-out for force majeure and hardware-driven SKU changes.
4) PO + signature timeline: require a signed PO and executed agreement by 2026-11-17. If PO not received, revert to standard published rates and no price guarantees.
5) Add minimum usage reporting and a quarterly sync for the first year to monitor economics.

Legal/Finance: please work the precise language and confirm no material accounting or revenue recognition issues with multi-year lock language. Once legal provides redlines, Sofia can share the updated SOW and DocuSign link with Greenline.

Ben
Ben Carter
SVP, Commercial Strategy | Redwood Inference
--

Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 15:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Three-year procurement question / budget constraints

Hi Sarah — good news: Ben greenlit the commercial structure with the exec conditions (summary below). 

What is approved (subject to legal redlines and PO by 11/17):
- Year 1 rate: $0.0048 / token equivalent with the committed $1.2M minimum over 36 months
- Uplift caps: up to 4% yoy for Years 2 and 3 (cumulative uplift across Y2–Y3 cannot exceed 8%)
- Renewal protection: limited early-renewal option if published list prices for the agreed model families increase more than 6% at renewal; exact trigger/definitions to be finalized by legal
- Operational requirements: quarterly usage reporting for first year and SOC2/audit-log confirmation (we have that in place)

Next steps: legal will send redlines to both parties today; I’ll circulate an updated SOW and a DocuSign link once we have approved language. To keep the commercial guarantee we need a signed PO + agreement by 2026-11-17. If procurement cannot commit to that timeline we’ll have to revert to published pricing without uplift guarantees.

Sarah — can you confirm Greenline can target PO + LOI by 11/17? If yes, I’ll fast-track legal and our DocuSign flow.

Thanks everyone — pushing to close this this week.

Best,
